newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich quoted as saying he might step aside.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich quoted as saying he might step aside.

text.p: Newt Gingrich said as recently as Friday that he would not rule out taking himself out of contention for re-election as House speaker, a fellow Republican House member said Sunday.

"That's right," Rep. Matt Salmon of Arizona said on the ABC program "This Week" in reply to a question about his description of a telephone conversation he said he had with Gingrich Friday about the possibility of stepping aside. "He said he was keeping his options open and that still might be a possibility."

Salmon said he had not discussed details of the circumstances under which Gingrich, the Georgia Republican who admitted Dec. 21 that he had broke House rules and brought discredit to the chamber, might step aside. On Monday, Gingrich is to address a meeting of House Republicans to seek their support for re-election Tuesday as speaker, the third-highest constitutional officer in the land.

"But it's still entirely possible that after Monday's conference, if the mood of the conference is along with my line of thinking, that we could elect another another speaker on Tuesday and have the understanding that in a month or two or whatever, however long it takes until we feel like we could get this resolved among ourselves that then the speaker could go back and we could have another election," Salmon said.
Salmon said he personally had encouraged Gingrich to step aside both for the good of the country and for Gingrich's own ultimate political good.
But he said he would vote for Gingrich if the speaker stuck to his plans to seek reelection rather than risk seeing House Democratic Leader Dick Gephardt of Missouri possibly be elected as speaker.
